subject: Copywriting
title: Dan Wieden: Just Do It
description: A quick win: understand Dan Wieden: Just Do It.

hook.text: Dan Wieden created 'Just Do It' for Nike in 1988. Inspired partly by a murderer's last words: 'Let's do it.'

buildup.text: Wieden and Kennedy founded their agency in Portland, far from Madison Avenue. Distance bred originality.

discovery.text: The three-word slogan transcended shoes. It became a life philosophy. Nike's brand became bigger than its products.

twist.text: Wieden nearly didn't present it. He thought it was too simple. Nike's Phil Knight was lukewarm at first too.

climax.text: It ran for 35+ years across every medium. 'Just Do It' became the most recognized slogan in commercial history.

punchline.text: Three words, 35 years. Simplicity wins every time.

details.summary: Dan Wieden co-founded Wieden+Kennedy and created Nike's 'Just Do It' in 1988 — arguably the greatest advertising slogan ever written. He built W+K into the world's largest independent agency by insisting on creative excellence, long-term brand partnerships, and a culture of fearless experimentation.
details.whyItMatters: Wieden proved that an independent agency could outperform global networks by prioritizing creative bravery. His body's of work demonstrates the commercial value of unforgettable brand language.
takeaways: He created Nike's 'Just Do It' — one of history's most iconic slogans
Wieden+Kennedy became the largest independent ad agency globally
He championed long-term creative partnerships over project-based work

faq.question: How did Dan Wieden come up with 'Just Do It'?
faq.answer: Wieden has said the phrase was partly inspired by convicted murderer Gary Gilmore's last words — 'Let's do it.' He modified it to 'Just Do It,' which captured Nike's ethos of pushing through hesitation. He later called it a lucky accident.

faq.question: What made Wieden+Kennedy successful as an independent agency?
faq.answer: W+K refused to be acquired by holding companies, maintaining creative independence. This attracted brands seeking bold, unconventional work. Their long-term Nike relationship proved that consistency and trust produce better creative than competitive agency reviews.
